transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is... I just don't really feel like myself anymore. I barely talk to anyone lately. I just kind of go flat and quiet. And at work—I'm a building cleaner—even just getting started on my cleaning route feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I just don't have it in me.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Not really, no. I used to look forward to a few things, like going fishing on Saturdays, or just sitting with a cup of coffee and doing the crossword puzzle. I even used to enjoy showing the younger guys at work some tricks for stripping a floor. But now... I mostly just let all those things sit. Doing them just doesn't give me anything back anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns lately?
Not really, no. My sleep has been pretty much the same as it always is. I just go to bed and wake up for my shift like usual. I haven't noticed any real changes there.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?

Yeah, I have. Most days... food just kind of tastes like cardboard to me now. I end up skipping meals, or maybe I'll just eat a few crackers after my shift is over. I guess I'm losing weight from it, too, because my work pants have been hanging a lot looser on me than they used to.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to, or having trouble sitting still?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm moving around at work, pushing the mop and doing my rounds at about the same pace I always do. I haven't noticed feeling slowed down or anything. And I don't have any trouble just sitting still, either.
Have you been having any thoughts that you've let people down or that you're a failure?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep thinking I failed everybody by losing my old place and not keeping my life together like I should have. It weighs on me a lot. It even gets to the point where, if the church pantry is short on supplies, or even if a hallway just gets missed at work... I somehow feel like that's on me, too. Like it's my fault.
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself?

Well, I don't have some big plan to do it or anything. But... yeah, a lot of mornings I wake up and just think that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. And honestly, having those thoughts... it scares me enough to actually say it out loud to you.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, the depression part... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. It started up not long after I had to move.
Have you had any periods in the last two weeks where you felt slightly better, even if only for a few hours?
No, not really. It's just... it's been pretty constant. I haven't really had any breaks from it, not even for a little while.
Do you feel noticeably worse in the morning?

Not really. I know I mentioned waking up with those thoughts, but the actual feeling... it doesn't seem noticeably worse in the morning compared to the rest of the day. It just stays pretty much the same from the time I get up until I go to sleep.
Do you feel like you're able to experience any pleasure at all, even if it's just for a brief moment, when good things happen to you?

No, I really don't. I used to... well, I used to look forward to things. Like going fishing on Saturdays, or just doing crosswords with a cup of coffee. Even at work, I used to enjoy showing the younger guys tricks for stripping a floor. 

But now I mostly just let those things sit. I don't really bother with them because... they just don't give me anything back anymore. So even if something good happens, I don't feel any pleasure from it, not even for a minute.
Do you feel like you're restless or fidgety, or that you have an inability to sit still?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel restless or fidgety. Honestly, it's more the opposite... I just sit there most of the time. I don't have any trouble staying still.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating on tasks or making decisions?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed any trouble concentrating. I can still focus on things fine when I need to, and making decisions hasn't been any harder than usual. It's just... I don't care much about doing any of it, you know? But the actual ability to focus is still there.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to in your daily activities?

No, I wouldn't say I'm moving any slower. I mean, I'm 59, so I'm not running any marathons, especially after being on my feet all day at work. But... no, my actual speed of doing things hasn't really changed. I just don't have the motivation to do much, but when I do get up to do something, I move at my normal pace.
Do you find yourself pacing back and forth or engaging in other repetitive movements when you're feeling down?

No, I don't really do that either. I don't pace around or... tap my foot or anything like that when I'm feeling down. Like I said, I mostly just sit. I don't really have the urge to move around much at all.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling like you need to be in constant motion when you're sitting still?
No, I don't get fidgety. I don't feel like I need to be moving around. If I'm sitting still, I'm just sitting still. There's no restless feeling or anything like that pushing me to move.
Would you say your depression is mild, moderate, or severe?

I'd say it's moderate. It's definitely there, and it makes things harder, but... it's not so severe that I can't function at all. I still go to work and get through the day. It just feels like a heavy weight I'm carrying around.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in, even if it's just a little bit?

Not really, no. I mean... I used to look forward to things. Like going fishing on Saturdays, or just sitting down to do the crosswords with a cup of coffee. Even at work, I used to enjoy showing the younger guys tricks for stripping a floor. But now... I mostly just let those things sit. I don't really bother with them because they just don't give me anything back anymore. So, no, I don't really get any enjoyment out of much right now.
Are there any small things that still bring you a tiny bit of joy or happiness?

Like I was just saying... no, not really. Even the small stuff. I used to look forward to getting my coffee and doing the crossword, or going fishing on Saturdays. Or even just showing the younger guys at work some tricks for stripping a floor. But I mostly just let all that sit now. None of it gives me anything back anymore. So, no, I don't really get even a tiny bit of joy out of things right now.
Can you think of any activity that you used to enjoy, but now you don't, and if so, did you lose interest in it suddenly or was it a gradual process?

Well, like I was just saying, it's exactly those things I mentioned. Fishing on Saturdays, doing the crosswords with my coffee, or showing the younger guys at work how to strip a floor. I used to really look forward to all of that. 

As to whether it was sudden or gradual... I guess I didn't really wake up one day and just stop. It just kind of faded out. I just started letting those things sit more and more, because... well, like I said, they just don't give me anything back anymore.
